scenes.headline: One server move. Customer data exposed.
scenes.body: How a trusted certificate company left a door open
scenes.say: DigiCert customers had data and some ID documents exposed. One server move left a door open for more than a year. Here is how it happened.

scenes.headline: A certificate authority, the company behind website trust
scenes.body: It issues the digital certificates browsers use to trust websites. Its business customers were affected.
scenes.say: DigiCert is a certificate authority. It issues the digital certificates that browsers use to trust websites. This time, its business customers were the ones affected.

scenes.headline: From server move to confirmation

items.text: Internal system moved; now reachable from the internet
Strange outside accounts spotted, judged harmless
Archived customer data read, until July 2
Data access confirmed; reported days later

scenes.say: In February twenty twenty-five, an internal system was moved, and it became reachable from the internet. On June eighteenth this year, staff spotted strange outside accounts, but judged them harmless. From June twenty-seventh to July second, an unauthorized account read archived customer data. DigiCert only confirmed that data access on October nineteenth.

scenes.headline: The move skipped a security review
scenes.body: It was treated as an infrastructure change, not a security change
scenes.say: Root cause number one: the move skipped a security review. DigiCert says it was treated as an infrastructure change, not a security change.

scenes.headline: Anyone could sign up, with no MFA
scenes.body: A self-registration feature let outsiders create accounts without multi-factor authentication
scenes.say: Root cause number two: a self-registration feature could be reached from outside. Outsiders could create their own accounts, with no multi-factor authentication.

scenes.headline: New accounts could read the archive
scenes.body: Accounts with no assigned app still got read-only access, and no alert fired on new sign-ups
scenes.say: Root cause number three: those new accounts had no app assigned, yet they could still read the archive. And no alert fired when strangers signed up.

scenes.headline: between the server move and the first warning sign
scenes.say: That is about sixteen months between the server move and the first warning sign.

scenes.headline: Business contact details, and some ID documents
scenes.body: Names, business emails, phone numbers, addresses · a small minority: passports, driving licences, utility bills
scenes.say: What was exposed? Mostly names, business emails, phone numbers and business addresses. For a small minority, identity documents too, like passports, driving licences or utility bills.

scenes.headline: How many people? Not disclosed.
scenes.body: DigiCert reported it to law enforcement and says it has no evidence of misuse
scenes.say: DigiCert has not said how many customers were affected. It reported the incident to law enforcement, and says it has no evidence the information was misused.

scenes.headline: No certificate operations were impacted.
scenes.body: DigiCert incident report · customers do not need to replace certificates
scenes.say: The good news: in DigiCert's words, no certificate operations were impacted. Certificates and logins were not affected, so customers do not need to replace their certificates.

scenes.headline: Network walls are not permissions.
scenes.body: If a system is safe only because it is hidden, one move can expose it.
scenes.say: Analyst note: network walls are not permissions. If a system is safe only because it is hidden, one move can expose it.

scenes.headline: Four lessons
items: Treat every network change as a security change
Check permissions in the app, not just the network
Alert on new accounts and unusual traffic
Watch for phishing that uses your business details
scenes.say: Four lessons. Treat every network change as a security change. Check permissions in the app, not just the network. Alert on new accounts and unusual traffic. And if you are a customer, watch for phishing that uses your business details.
